_about: (ARCHITECTURE x ENGINE) support, the fact class the campaign did not key. Every row was paid for with a lost pair.
_why: Capability is recorded as (model x environment) in data/model_load_environments.json, and every checkpoint below LOADS FINE under transformers. The engine is a separate axis: vLLM has removed architectures it once shipped, never implemented others, ships a broken loader for one, and hosts one correctly at a tenth of the speed. No preflight, no load record and no fidelity guard could see any of it. The passage-corpus run lost 11% of its declared population to this in a single afternoon.
_read_by: scripts/vllm_engine_preflight.py — run it BEFORE a fleet launches, not after a box fails.
_error_shape: REMOVED architectures fail as a pydantic ValidationError at ModelConfig, before weights load, and the message names the last working version. Read it: it is a specification, not a complaint.
_maintenance: When a box teaches you something, add the row IN THE SAME SESSION. Absence of an observation is not evidence of support.

RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.note: Hosted CORRECTLY and roughly 10x slow: ~255 output tok/s, 25-28% GPU utilisation, ~10h for a pair against ~1h for a dense 7B on the same card. Griffin's recurrent layers give the scheduler almost nothing to batch.
RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.recovery: Nothing to fix. Treat as a PACKING WEIGHT alongside VRAM — packed by pair count or sequence count alone, one recurrent pair becomes the whole fleet's tail.
RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.do_not: Do NOT restart it for low utilisation. 25% is not the 0%-twice torch.compile signature, and a pair writes all its rows only at the very end, so a restart discards the entire pair.
RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.ROOT_CAUSE_RESEARCHED_20260812: vLLM HAS NO NATIVE RECURRENTGEMMA IMPLEMENTATION AT ANY VERSION. `RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM` is absent from vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py at v0.27.1 and at every version checked back to v0.4.1, and absent from the explicit _TRANSFORMERS_BACKEND_MODELS allow-list. When an architecture is not in the registry and model_impl=='auto' (the DEFAULT), resolve_model_cls falls through to _try_resolve_transformers(), which pulls the class from the installed `transformers` package and runs it via TransformersForCausalLM. vLLM's own docs state there is NO WARNING that this is fallback behaviour. So we were never running vLLM's code -- we were running HuggingFace's reference PyTorch, whose RG-LRU scan is a literal per-timestep Python loop (`for t in range(...): recurrent_states = gate[:,t]*recurrent_states + x[:,t]`). Google's own recurrentgemma repo says the FLAX path uses a low-level Pallas fused kernel and the PyTorch one is 'un-optimized... for reference'.
RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.why_the_symptoms_fit: Sequential small-kernel launches are launch-bound, not compute-bound: the card idles between hundreds of tiny elementwise kernels, which is exactly a steady 20-28% utilisation. And SCORING is disproportionately worse than generation because prompt_logprobs teacher-forcing is pure PREFILL over the full stored sequence -- entirely the O(seq_len) loop, with no O(1)-per-token decode phase to amortise it.
RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.cheap_wins: NONE FOUND. Batch width does not reduce the number of sequential timesteps. VLLM_USE_V1 targets the native hybrid/Mamba cache path, which this model never enters because it is not registered at all.
RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.alternatives: JAX/Flax official repo is the ONLY path with a source-confirmed FUSED kernel (Pallas). MLX has recurrentgemma.py but with the SAME Python-loop scan, and its batch_generate does not expose per-token logprobs (open issue ml-explore/mlx-lm#1358). llama.cpp does NOT support the architecture at all (issue #6564 closed unimplemented; llama-arch.cpp has no Griffin entry). HF transformers directly is the same code vLLM already falls back to.
RecurrentGemmaForCausalLM.unknown: Whether the Pallas RG-LRU kernel runs on non-TPU. And NO public RecurrentGemma GPU tokens/sec figure exists anywhere, so our ~255 tok/s is uncompared.

Zamba2ForCausalLM.recovery: transformers==4.57.1 AND mamba-ssm + causal-conv1d kernels (19.3x on the sibling architecture) AND base-arm repo access. Three requirements, each individually satisfiable, never yet tried together.
Zamba2ForCausalLM.blocked_on: The base arm returns a gated-repo OSError against a published Apache-2.0 licence on an ungated family. The ALIGNED arm is demonstrated locally.

tokenizer_class._note: NOT architecture x engine — these load and host fine and die in TOKENIZATION or DETOKENIZATION. Kept here because the operational question ('will this fleet lose the pair?') is the same one.

sentencepiece_out_of_range.error: IndexError: OUT_OF_RANGE: piece id is out of range — self._processor.IdToPiece(id)
sentencepiece_out_of_range.cause: The cross-scoring guard dropped on the MODEL's vocab size (embedding rows, routinely padded) while the crash is in the TOKENIZER's piece count. An id can sit under the padding, pass the guard, and still kill the run.
sentencepiece_out_of_range.recovery: FIXED in scripts/vllm_y_run.py: the bound is min(model_vocab, len(tokenizer)). Re-run both pairs.
sentencepiece_out_of_range.caveat: The corrected guard drops strictly MORE than the old one, so pairs collected before the fix ran under a looser bound. Declared in amendment §1e.
sentencepiece_out_of_range.fixed_note: Bound corrected to min(model_vocab, len(tokenizer)) in scripts/vllm_y_run.py at 01d8668cf1b6. A box must be running code at or after this commit -- the runner is pulled by `git pull` at launch, so an already-running box does NOT have it.

measured_padding._note: MEASURED on the box 12 Aug, not inferred. The gap between embedding rows and tokenizer pieces IS the defect: every id in it passes a model-vocab guard and crashes IdToPiece.

sentencepiece_out_of_range.fix_is_load_bearing: CONFIRMED by measurement rather than by the run completing. Three of the four arms have a real padding gap, so the corrected min() bound differs from the old one and the ids it newly excludes are exactly the ones that raise IdToPiece. Teuken's INSTRUCT arm has no gap -- the pair is protected by its BASE arm's bound, which is why a per-pair check must look at both arms and not one.
sentencepiece_out_of_range.how_to_check_any_pair: len(AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(m)) < AutoConfig.from_pretrained(m).vocab_size -> the pair is exposed. Cheap, needs no weights, and answers it before a box is rented.
sentencepiece_out_of_range.fix_DEMONSTRATED: OBSERVED FIRING 12 Aug on Teuken: '723/4096 dropped: id >= scorer vocab 250680'. 250,680 is the TOKENIZER's piece count; the old guard would have used the base arm's 250,880 embedding rows, let those 723 sequences through, and raised IdToPiece. This is the fix doing the work, not the pair getting lucky.
sentencepiece_out_of_range.ct_llm_did_NOT_exercise_it: CT-LLM completed with ZERO drop lines. Its recovery is therefore NOT evidence for the fix -- different box, different card, different sampled ids. Two pairs recovered, only ONE of them tests the guard. Do not cite CT-LLM as confirmation.
sentencepiece_out_of_range.cost_of_correctness: ~17.6% of sequences dropped in the observed chunk. The fix converts a CRASH into MISSINGNESS, which is the right trade but is not free: expect Teuken to carry a high unscorable rate, in the Aquila2 class rather than the 0.03% corpus norm. Per-pair denominators, not the corpus mean.

detokenizer_none.error: TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not iterable — for ch in raw_token
detokenizer_none.cause: vLLM's incremental detokenizer receives None for a token. Distinct from the transformers-v5 #45488 prompt-mangling defect that LOADER_OVERRIDE addresses — that one is about the PROMPT, this one is about the OUTPUT.
detokenizer_none.recovery: Generate with detokenize=False and decode from full_ids with the HF tokenizer under LOADER_OVERRIDE. The ids are already stored, so nothing is lost.
detokenizer_none.note: The pre-run amendment predicted this pair would collect, arguing from the beam_fc corpus that its TOKENIZER is fine. That argument still stands and was about a different stage. Collectable in one stack is not collecting in another.

_FOURTH_KIND: SILENT FALLBACK is a fourth (architecture x engine) kind, and the most dangerous because nothing announces it: a model absent from vLLM's registry is not refused, it is quietly run through the generic Transformers backend with no warning. It loads, it is correct, and it is unfused. Check membership in vllm/model_executor/models/registry.py, not whether the model loads.

_REGISTRY_AUDIT_20260812.method: ModelRegistry.get_supported_archs() read from the RUNNING box (vLLM 0.27.1, 367 architectures), joined against AutoConfig.architectures for all 92 corpus checkpoints. 0 unresolved.
_REGISTRY_AUDIT_20260812.THE_DISTINCTION_THE_REGISTRY_CANNOT_MAKE: Absence from the registry produces TWO different behaviours and the registry does not say which. Aquila / Baichuan / jais were REMOVED and raise a pydantic ValidationError naming the last working version. Pharia and RWKV raise 'not supported for now'. recurrentgemma FELL BACK SILENTLY and ran. Ten of the twelve announced themselves; ONE did not. So registry membership predicts 'not native', not 'will fail' -- and the only way we learned which was to run it.
_REGISTRY_AUDIT_20260812.reassurance: NO HIDDEN FALLBACK among the 41 collected pairs. recurrentgemma is the sole silent case in this corpus.
_REGISTRY_AUDIT_20260812.do_this_next_fleet: Run this join BEFORE launching: any checkpoint absent from get_supported_archs() is either going to fail loudly or run unfused, and both are worth knowing in advance.
